senses.d: Right; on the right-hand side. (In heraldry, specifically the bearer's right, which is the viewer's left.)
ex: my Mothers bloud / Runs on the dexter checke, and this ſiniſter / Bounds in my fathers:
Clovis wiped the trace of Turkish coffee and the beginnings of a smile from his lips, and slowly lowered his dexter eyelid.

senses.d: The right side (of a building, an equation, a heraldic shield [from the wearer's perspective], etc).
ex: On the dexter of the court is a long hall with an arched ceiling and a door, leading to a small oblong shrine with a vaulted ceiling.

pt:destro.gl: right-handed (more skillful with one’s right hand)

ety.text: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese destro, from Latin dextrum. Cognate with Galician destro, and Spanish diestro. Doublet of Dexter.
